one_line: Visual multi-cloud infrastructure CAD with claimed WebMCP co-design and Terraform generation.
what_it_does: Lets humans and external agents design cloud topologies on a node canvas and claims Terraform and audit workflows.
leverage_rationale: Structured canvas state and atomic architecture mutations could materially improve agent precision, but the frames do not make tool use or the claimed Terraform/audit result legible.
leverage_evidence: Frame sheets show a progressively populated connected node/workflow canvas.
Devpost packaging claims typed tools, live spatial state, Terraform compilation, and audits.
execution_rationale: The product UI appears real and increasingly populated, but evidence is too low-resolution and lacks an end-to-end readable result.
execution_evidence: Multiple frame sheets show a dark canvas editor with nodes and connectors.
No readable completion, Terraform output, or audit result is visible.
impact_rationale: Cloud architecture design, cost, and security review are substantial problems for a clear professional audience.
impact_evidence: Packaging targets AWS/Azure/GCP topology design and production infrastructure concerns.
About text identifies drift, security misconfiguration, and budget blowouts.
creativity_rationale: Combining spatial infrastructure CAD, external agent co-design, and multi-agent SecOps/FinOps is ambitious and distinctive.
creativity_evidence: Claimed human plus four-role agent swarm collaboration.
Multi-cloud visual-to-Terraform concept is a fresh hackathon synthesis.
usability_note: The canvas concept is plausible, but the submitted frames are visually sparse and hard to interpret.
red_flags: No submitted video despite media-like frame sheets.
Claims such as production Terraform and zero race conditions are not visibly verified.

one_line: Compiles a human-selected, expiring field-level delegation into a live WebMCP tool.
what_it_does: A CRM workflow lets a person delegate exact records and fields for a fixed duration; the server re-checks every agent call and keeps apply human-only.
leverage_rationale: The live tool is generated from current human intent, scoped to exact records/fields and expiry, and enforced server-side on every call; this is substantially beyond UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows a mandate created for two records, two fields, and ten minutes.
Transcript shows in-scope staging, out-of-scope rejection, no agent apply tool, and server-side re-checking.
execution_rationale: The long video transcript gives a coherent end-to-end workflow with visible state, rejection, staging, and human commit boundary; minor uncertainty remains because frame text is small.
execution_evidence: Transcript documents select, grant, live tool creation, accepted call, rejected call, and human-only apply.
Frame sheets show the CRM/workbench and evolving agent panel states.
impact_rationale: Temporary, least-privilege delegation addresses a real and important problem in agent access control for business records.
impact_evidence: The demonstrated scenario grants only selected fields on selected customer accounts.
The design prevents stale or overbroad credentials and keeps consequential commit with the person.
creativity_rationale: Treating a momentary natural-language permission as a compiled, expiring WebMCP capability is a highly original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Devpost packaging explicitly frames Mandate as a compiler from human intent to a live tool contract.
Exact record/field enums and expiry are part of the demonstrated concept.
usability_note: The workflow provides scope readback, persistent mandate indicators, and a clear human apply boundary.
red_flags: Some claims rely on a narrated demo rather than independently observed runtime access.
standouts: Strongest evidence-backed WebMCP-specific leverage in the packet.
Human authorization is deliberately separated from agent preparation.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage, coherent execution evidence, and a novel security interaction make this a clear advancement.

one_line: A governed gateway inspects WebMCP tools and outputs before allowing agent actions.
what_it_does: Screens metadata and returned data, minimizes parameters, requires approval for mutations, and records an auditable trust log.
leverage_rationale: A structured mediation layer can inspect tool schemas and outputs, minimize data, and enforce per-call consent more reliably than generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Frame sheets show connected tools, an agent task, trust log, and a red approval/quarantine state.
Packaging visibly claims poisoned output was quarantined before reaching the agent and zero sensitive fields sent.
execution_rationale: The storyboard consistently shows configuration, task invocation, trust logging, warning/quarantine, and approval states, though much is presented as a thumbnail/demo package.
execution_evidence: Frames show enabled integrations, a run action, populated trust log, and guarded mutation UI.
Devpost screenshot shows concrete dashboard labels and counters.
impact_rationale: Prompt injection, data minimization, and human approval are central safety problems for agent-enabled websites.
impact_evidence: The product targets poisoned tool output and unnecessary sensitive-field transmission.
The flow explicitly avoids automatic cancellation and requires one-call approval.
creativity_rationale: The combination of tool metadata inspection, output sanitization, parameter minimization, and consent auditing is a thoughtful security-layer synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Five-control gateway model is clearly articulated.
The demo centers on a clean-looking tool returning malicious instructions.
usability_note: The three-panel connected-tools/task/trust-log layout makes governance legible.
red_flags: Most numeric counters and attack claims are visible as promotional UI rather than independently verifiable runtime evidence.
standouts: Clear trust log and quarantine interaction.
Human approval is scoped to one mutation call.
advance_reason: Strong impact and concrete governance workflow justify advancement despite packaging-heavy evidence.

one_line: Turns a brain dump into a source-bound, inspectable, human-approved decision proposal.
what_it_does: Browser agents read a current source, stage structured amplification tied to revision/fingerprint, and leave approval to the human UI.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes shared structured source/workspace state and enables stale-write rejection, which improves repeatability and provenance beyond UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies read, stage, and workspace tools sharing live state.
It claims revision/fingerprint binding and rejection of stale writes.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a detailed product contract, but submitted frames are low-resolution and do not clearly prove the full decision workflow or result.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show repeated dark multi-panel task/workspace interfaces.
No readable final proposal, source excerpt, or stale-write error is visible.
impact_rationale: Decision support with source grounding and human approval has clear value for knowledge workers and research/planning tasks.
impact_evidence: The stated workflow includes facts, assumptions, unknowns, trade-offs, recommendation, and reversal condition.
It is presented as subject-independent across decision modes.
creativity_rationale: Binding agent-generated decision structure to exact source revision and exposing an auditable shared workspace is a fresh interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The app makes itself the test decision and uses source fingerprints as a core concept.
Human approval is intentionally outside the agent tool surface.
usability_note: The intended structure is strong, but the visual evidence is too dense and illegible to assess polish.
red_flags: No video submitted and frame text is not legible.
standouts: Source revision/fingerprint binding is a meaningful integrity mechanism.
advance_reason: High conceptual leverage and impact merit advancement, but execution should be verified in a later stage.

one_line: An open-source Chrome side-panel browser agent stack for WebMCP builders.
what_it_does: Provides an experimental agentic Chrome session using WebMCP, LangGraph.js, MCP, and semantic browser automation.
leverage_rationale: A side-panel agent with semantic access to WebMCP tools can reduce browser-driving friction for builders, but the packet does not show specific tool execution clearly.
leverage_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows a Chrome side panel alongside a WebMCP-themed site.
About text claims real Chrome-session operation and open-source agent stack.
execution_rationale: There are no submitted frame sheets, and the only screenshot is a paused Devpost media preview with mostly illegible side-panel text.
execution_evidence: No video frame sheets submitted.
Packaging screenshot shows a paused embedded demo, not runtime behavior.
impact_rationale: Builders have a real need for practical WebMCP experimentation and semantic browser automation tooling.
impact_evidence: The project is explicitly aimed at builders and an emerging browser-agent development workflow.

creativity_rationale: A real Chrome side-panel agent combining WebMCP and semantic automation is a useful, moderately original developer-tool synthesis.
creativity_evidence: The concept exposes the future dual human/agent web interface through a builder-oriented side panel.
It combines WebMCP with LangGraph.js and MCP.
usability_note: The concept is plausible but the packet gives too little legible evidence to assess actual usability.
red_flags: No frame sheets or video evidence submitted.
Description contains malformed punctuation and broad claims.
standouts: Targets real Chrome sessions rather than a purely abstract agent demo.
advance_reason: Potentially useful infrastructure, but evidence is too thin for advancement in a blind Stage 1 review.

one_line: A claimed zero-trust context middleware for sanitizing and encrypting WebMCP context.
what_it_does: Claims DOM context interception, WASM/SIMD sanitization, WebCrypto worker isolation, edge policies, and provenance signing.
leverage_rationale: If implemented, context interception and policy enforcement would materially improve agent safety, but WebMCP behavior is not demonstrated.
leverage_evidence: About text lists context interception, prompt-injection sanitization, PII tokenization, and policy enforcement.
The packet claims native context integration rather than merely exposing a button.
execution_rationale: The live demo is dead, no frame sheets were submitted, and the Devpost screenshot shows a private video, leaving no runtime evidence.
execution_evidence: FACTS report demo_alive=dead.
Packaging screenshot says the embedded video is private.
No direct product or result view is visible.
impact_rationale: Prompt injection and PII leakage in agent context are real, high-consequence problems for developers and organizations.
impact_evidence: Project targets sanitization, encryption, and edge policy enforcement for browser context.
The stated threat model concerns indirect PII exfiltration.
creativity_rationale: Combining DOM-aware sanitization, worker-isolated cryptography, and edge policy distribution is ambitious, though mostly claim-level here.
creativity_evidence: WASM/SIMD plus WebCrypto isolation and signed context provenance are an unusual combined architecture claim.
usability_note: No usable runtime surface is available to assess.
standouts: Addresses a serious agent-context security threat model.
advance_reason: The security idea is relevant, but there is no runtime evidence to support execution or eligibility confidence.

what_it_does: Lets agents negotiate price, quantity, freebies, shipping, and coupons across a product catalog, then presents a human confirm step.
leverage_rationale: Negotiating structured offers over several rounds with shared buyer/seller state is a strong WebMCP use case and materially more precise than generic UI driving.

execution_evidence: Frames show landing page, catalog loading/population, and product-detail loading states.

creativity_evidence: The concept treats a deal as a negotiated bundle of terms.
The implementation claims a single mutation path enforcing buyer budget and seller floor.
usability_note: Catalog and filters are visible, but the negotiation and confirmation UX are not shown end-to-end.

one_line: An agent finds and holds a dental consultation slot, then books only after human approval.
what_it_does: Exposes tools for service discovery, availability, ten-minute holds, approval, confirmation, and dental inbox status.
leverage_rationale: Shared calendar state plus explicit hold and one-time confirmation tools make booking safer and more reliable than an agent guessing through forms.
leverage_evidence: About text lists find, hold, approval, confirm, and status workflow.

impact_evidence: The workflow targets real dental consultation booking and clinic inbox handoff.
Shared state and explicit confirmation reduce booking errors and unauthorized commitments.
creativity_rationale: Agent-assisted booking with holds and human confirmation is a thoughtful, well-executed application, though the category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Ten-minute holds and one-time approval token are meaningful interaction details.

usability_note: The visible intake, calendar, and review flow is understandable and action-oriented.

one_line: A governed WebMCP refund workflow using Human GO, single-use permits, verified readback, and replay denial.
what_it_does: Agents inspect a synthetic duplicate-charge case and propose a refund; a human authorizes an exact permit, execution is verified, and replay is denied.
leverage_rationale: The product uses WebMCP as a precise authority surface: discovery and proposal are separated from human authorization, one-time execution, readback verification, and replay denial.
leverage_evidence: Frame sheets visibly show NO PROPOSAL YET, HUMAN_GO_REQUIRED, NOT EXECUTED, PERMIT_READY, and VERIFIED states.
Frames show a single-use permit and structured event/evidence areas.
Packaging claims eight native tools and replay mutation count zero.
execution_rationale: The storyboard visibly covers proposal, human gate, permit, execution/verification states, and exactly-once claims; some evidence is still presentation-oriented rather than live inspection.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show bounded duplicate-charge case, human-required state, permit readiness, verified readback, and exactly-once captions.
Devpost packaging presents a consistent synthetic €49 scenario and evidence receipt concept.
impact_rationale: Preventing unauthorized or replayed consequential mutations is a major problem for agent-enabled financial workflows, even in a synthetic demo.
impact_evidence: The workflow explicitly protects a refund mutation and keeps pre-approval mutations at zero.
Verified readback and replay denial address auditability and idempotency.
creativity_rationale: The explicit separation of discoverability, authority, bounded proposal, single-use permit, verified readback, and replay denial is a memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The repeated state-machine presentation makes authority—not intelligence—the core product concept.
Single-use permits and exact proposal binding are distinctive safeguards.
usability_note: State labels and evidence panels make the governance flow unusually legible.
red_flags: The packet’s strongest states are shown in a storyboard/presentation, so live backend enforcement remains to be checked.
standouts: Visible state machine includes both safe pre-GO containment and post-execution verification.
advance_reason: Top-tier WebMCP leverage and unusually concrete governed-execution evidence make this a clear advancement.
